macro.regime: Mechanical snapback inside an unresolved AI-capex-unwind regime
macro.narrative: Monday's violent snapback (S&P +4.73% to 7237.17, Nasdaq +6.51% to 24089.56, VIX -25.8% to 26.62) was driven overwhelmingly by a company-specific, mechanical catalyst -- Trump-pressured reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO, which sent NVDA up 31-34% in the largest single-day market-cap gain ever recorded, on forced short-covering and dealer hedge-unwinds -- rather than any resolution of the macro overhang, and Tuesday premarket futures (S&P +2.9%, Nasdaq100 +3.6%, Dow +2.1%) extended the move without yet confirming a trend change. Fed-funds futures actually priced the Dec 9 25bp hike higher on Monday, to roughly 97-98%, even as equities rallied -- a genuinely hawkish signal that Treasury Secretary Bessent's Sun 22 Nov overtightening warning has so far failed to move, while the 10yr sits little-changed near 4.95-4.96%. Credit has not round-tripped with equities: HY OAS remains pinned near 352bp and CCC spreads near the 100th percentile of their post-Oct-2023 range (~1,350bp+), with AI-linked credit (CoreWeave-type names) still distressed, so the capex-unwind-driven credit stress is still live beneath the surface. Nvidia's SEC accounting probe into its revenue-geography reporting is explicitly unresolved by Huang's reinstatement, and multiple sell-side voices (Capital Economics, Swissquote, and outlets describing the move as 'mechanical'/short-covering) are calling Monday a dead-cat bounce rather than an all-clear. Asia stabilization measures continue to escalate rather than wind down -- Taiwan's short-sale ban was its third intervention in three weeks (margin now 150%), China cut margin requirements to 80% effective Nov 30, and Korea is readying its own fund -- signaling authorities still see this as a live de-risking threat, not a resolved one.
